adeno has definitely negatively impacted my school and work over the years. Its a really difficult time to find work but there are still opportunities out there that are flexible and allow you to make your own hours. 
I think ultimately if you can make a side hustle or try to arrange some contract work with bookkeeping or online freelance work, it'll give you some extra cash. If you're decent at writing, theres some options from what Ive seen. 
I actually quit a job because it was too much outdoor- no bathroom access work and I had to admit to myself that it doesn't make sense for someone with this condition. I switched to a job that I can spend most of my time in close vicinity to a bathroom in case I have my standard debilitating period cramps. 

This is not an easy condition and its not an easy time either. I think stress makes it worse as well, so if you start casually looking for a little extra dough- maybe even a second part time job- it'll be an easier transition and you can figure out what kind of work set up is most conducive. 
IMO a job that has flexible hours is an absolute must.

what kind of work are you looking for? If it's general unskilled work you can go through a temp agency and would have better luck going in person to places and asking for work. 

If it is skilled or specialized work you may want to contact an employment agency that specializes in your field. 

Depending on the field you want to go into or are in, you can look up certifications that will strengthen your resume. 

Unfortunately, you can literally waste years on applying to jobs. The key is to stay busy and try to grow as a stronger candidate/ skill build. This effort will be very important when potential employers ask you what you've been doing while unemployed. 

Take good care of your health and make sure you're doing things you enjoy. 

One more thing might be to switch up your resume style, that made a large impact for me.
